subject: apollo astronaut
title: What If the First Moon Landing Had Failed? Nixon's Speech Was Already Written

scenes.text: What if Apollo 11 had failed? The speech for that night was already typed.
July 18, 1969, two days before the landing. Speechwriter William Safire hands in a memo: In Event of Moon Disaster.
The fear isn't a crash. It's two men alive on the Moon whose engine won't fire.
The President would phone the widows-to-be, then tell the world: fate has ordained that the men who went to the Moon to explore in peace will stay on the Moon to rest in peace.
Then NASA would cut communications, and a clergyman would commend their souls to the deepest of the deep, like a burial at sea.
The engine fired. And the memo sat unnoticed in the National Archives for thirty years.

description:
What if the first Moon landing had failed? The White House had a plan, and a speech.
On 18 July 1969, two days before Apollo 11 landed, speechwriter William Safire wrote a memo titled In Event of Moon Disaster for the case that Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin were stranded on the Moon. President Nixon was to telephone the widows-to-be, read a short address to the nation, and a clergyman was to follow the procedure for a burial at sea once NASA ended communications. The memo became public in 1999, thirty years later.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The speech ends with every person who looks up at the Moon knowing there is some corner of another world that is forever mankind. Which other close call should we run through?
